# Introduction:

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

import seaborn as sns

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = sns.load_dataset('iris')

sns.set_context('talk')
```

150 flowers we want to know correlation with sepal and petal with the species of flowers

Study whether pedal width correlates with pedal length

# Literature Review:



# Method:

Two columns of continuous data (length of petal and width of petal measured in millimeters) we will evaluate this relationship using simple correlation analysis and a scatterplot. These two methods are classic and traditional starting points when evaluating data like these.

# Results:

```{python}

corr_val = np.array(df[['petal_length' , 'petal_width']].corr())[0][1]

narrative = "a very strong negative correlation"

if corr_val>.8:
  narrative = "a very strong positive correlation"
elif corr_val >.4:
  narrative = "a moderate positive correlation"
elif corr_val > 0:
  narrative = "a positive but weak correlation"
elif corr_val > -.4:
  narrative = "a moderate negative correlation"
```
Using the class simple correlation approach these data produce a correlation coefficient of `{python} f"{corr_val:.5f}"`

Given this result we conclude that this relationship is `{python} f"{narrative}"`.


```{python}
#| label: fig-length-width-scatter
#| fig-cap: "a scatterplot of petal length and width"

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6,3.5))

sns.scatterplot(data=df, y='petal_length', x='petal_width')
sns.lmplot(data = df, y='petal_length', x='petal_width')
```
as shown in @fig-length-width-scatter

we found the correlation coefficient and plotted it. positive correlation between iris petal width and iris petal length
